crowned-heads--four-kicks.description: Four Kicks, a Crowned Heads blend named after a rock song, is made by E.P. Carrillo at Tabacalera La Alianza in the Dominican Republic. An Ecuadorian Habano wrapper covers Nicaraguan binder and filler aged at least eighteen months. Leather and damp earth carry the smoke, with pepper, a little cocoa and coffee, and a caramel-like sweetness that grows as it burns.

thirds.notes: Damp earth and oily leather lead, with pepper and spice and a hint of caramel on the retrohale.
The profile smooths out and the caramel-like sweetness becomes clearer on the draw.
Flavors hold steady while the strength climbs noticeably toward the end.

crowned-heads--mil-dias.description: Released in 2020, Mil Días is rolled at Tabacalera Pichardo in Estelí, Nicaragua, with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and long filler from Nicaragua, Peru and Costa Rica. Cedar and white pepper open onto a creamy core with earth, roasted nuts and baking spice; a balanced, layered smoke for an unhurried evening.

thirds.notes: Bold cedar and earth with a sharp black-pepper edge and a first hint of cream.
Pepper recedes as the smoke turns creamier, with smooth cedar, a nutty sweetness and a touch of cocoa.
Nutmeg and cinnamon come through the cream, with earth and leather as the strength builds.

crowned-heads--headley-grange.description: Headley Grange is a Crowned Heads blend made by E.P. Carrillo, pairing an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler. Wood and spice carry the smoke, softened by a dried-fruit sweetness and later by cream and cocoa, before nutmeg and pepper return at the close; a warming cigar for after dinner.

thirds.notes: Woody notes and a burst of pepper lead, easing into a light sweetness like dried apricot.
Spiced wood stays in front while cocoa and cream build around the midpoint.
Nutmeg and spice rise again over the wood, with toast and a little leather at the finish.

crowned-heads--le-careme.description: Introduced in 2016 and named for the French chef Marie-Antoine Carême, Le Carême is made at Tabacalera La Alianza in the Dominican Republic: a dark Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper, an Ecuadorian Sumatra binder and Nicaraguan filler. Cocoa and pepper open the smoke, later joined by cream and cedar, with a faint saline note and a dry, espresso-like finish.

thirds.notes: Red and black pepper over chocolate and natural tobacco, with touches of cedar and dark fruit.
The pepper calms; a creamy, latte-like character and cedar settle around the chocolate.
Cocoa holds on as earthy, mineral and salty notes appear, ending on a bitter espresso edge.

crowned-heads--la-imperiosa.description: La Imperiosa, launched in 2015, puts the blend of the 2014 Las Calaveras limited edition into regular production. It is rolled at My Father Cigars in Estelí, with a dark, oily Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. Pepper gives way to dark fruit and chocolate, then leather and cedar; a rich, sweet-edged smoke for the evening.

thirds.notes: Pepper at the light quickly makes room for plum- and raisin-like fruit and dark chocolate.
Leather moves to the front with cedar, espresso and earth, the fruit staying in the background.
Chocolate and roasted nuts deepen while red pepper and heat build toward the end.

crowned-heads--le-patissier.description: Shown at the 2021 trade show, Le Pâtissier is the broadleaf branch of the Le Carême family, made at Tabacalera Pichardo in Estelí. A Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper covers a Jalapa binder and filler from Costa Rica and Nicaragua's Ometepe and Pueblo Nuevo. Coffee, dark chocolate and stone-fruit sweetness lead, with pepper building toward a long finish; a cigar for the dessert course.

thirds.notes: Roasted coffee and dark chocolate with a fruity, sugary sweetness and a lingering black-pepper finish.
The coffee drifts toward cocoa, softened by whipped cream and lifted by anise-like spice.
Dense chocolate and black coffee with a touch of earth, as the pepper grows into a long finish.

crowned-heads--juarez.description: Juarez followed Crowned Heads' Jericho Hill and is made at Tabacalera Pichardo in Nicaragua. An earthy Mexican San Andrés wrapper is laid over an Ecuadorian Sumatra binder and long filler from the Dominican Republic and Nicaragua. The smoke leans on chocolate, leather and earth, with black pepper, oak and sweet spice around the edges.
